title: AI can improve financial-service quality and efficiency
claim: AI can improve personalised financial advice, credit-risk assessment, customer support and claims handling.
evidence: BIS describes AI as having substantial potential to improve quality and efficiency across these financial-service activities.
strategic_implication: FinNova should evaluate AI across risk, lending and customer operations rather than treating AI as only a chatbot capability.

title: AI can strengthen fraud detection and transaction security
claim: AI can strengthen fraud detection and improve transaction security.
evidence: BIS explicitly identifies fraud detection and transaction security among potential benefits of AI in finance.
strategic_implication: Fraud prevention is a credible high-value AI transformation candidate for FinNova.

title: AI adoption is expanding across financial-sector functions
claim: Financial firms are adopting AI in internal productivity, customer-facing functions, credit decision support and fraud detection.
evidence: BIS reports concentrated adoption in text analysis, classification, information search and customer-facing functions, alongside experimentation in credit decision support and fraud detection.
strategic_implication: FinNova's transformation roadmap should distinguish low-risk productivity use cases from higher-risk core decisioning use cases.

title: Generative AI can support document analysis and customer engagement
claim: Generative AI creates opportunities for document analysis and customer-service assistance.
evidence: BIS discusses GenAI for broader data analysis, document analysis for credit underwriting and AI-powered customer-service chatbots.
strategic_implication: FinNova could use GenAI for document-heavy lending workflows and support augmentation before deploying autonomous decisions.

title: AI can support operational efficiency and compliance
claim: AI can improve operational efficiency in back-office processes, KYC and loan processing.
evidence: RBI Deputy Governor T Rabi Sankar's BIS speech identifies operational efficiency, KYC, loan processing and customer support as AI opportunities.
strategic_implication: FinNova should consider process automation as a measurable transformation outcome.

title: Digital payments account for most reported fraud cases by number
claim: Frauds occurred predominantly in digital payments such as card/internet transactions in terms of number.
evidence: RBI's Annual Report 2024-25 states that frauds were predominantly in digital payments by number.
strategic_implication: Because FinNova operates digital payments, fraud detection should be evaluated as a core strategic capability.

title: Loan portfolios dominate fraud value
claim: Frauds were reported primarily in the loan portfolio in terms of value.
evidence: RBI reports advances as the largest area by value among fraud cases in its cited reporting period.
strategic_implication: FinNova's lending business creates a second major risk dimension, making combined fraud-and-lending intelligence strategically relevant.

title: Fraud detection can suffer from long detection delays
claim: RBI identified a significant time lag between occurrence and detection of reported frauds.
evidence: The RBI annual report notes that a very large share of fraud value reported in the year related to frauds occurring in previous financial years.
strategic_implication: Reducing detection latency is a defensible transformation KPI for FinNova's fraud programme.

title: AI can identify suspicious transaction networks
claim: Graph-based AI approaches can improve fraud detection by identifying suspicious transaction networks.
evidence: BIS discusses graph neural networks for suspicious transaction-network detection and cross-border fraud monitoring.
strategic_implication: FinNova can consider network-aware fraud analytics as a future capability beyond simple transaction rules.

title: AI is already used for fraud and cyber-risk mitigation
claim: Surveyed firms reported AI use for cyber-attack, fraud and money-laundering risk mitigation.
evidence: BIS reported 37% of respondents using AI against cyber-attack, 33% for fraud and 20% for money laundering.
strategic_implication: Fraud AI is not merely speculative; it is an established financial-sector use case.

title: AI-enabled scams are becoming more sophisticated
claim: Financial scams are becoming more sophisticated and increasingly leverage AI and deepfakes.
evidence: OECD notes that growing online financial-service use increases fraud exposure and that AI/deepfakes are contributing to more sophisticated scams.
strategic_implication: FinNova needs adaptive fraud controls and customer education, not only static rules.

title: Digital lending requires need-based data collection and explicit consent
claim: Digital lending data collection must be need-based and based on prior explicit borrower consent with an audit trail.
evidence: RBI Digital Lending Guidelines specify these requirements and provide borrowers options around consent and data use.
strategic_implication: Any AI lending architecture for FinNova must include consent, purpose limitation and auditable data use.

title: Algorithmic features in digital lending require transparency
claim: Algorithmic features used in digital lending should be documented to ensure necessary transparency.
evidence: RBI's digital-lending working-group recommendations include documentation of algorithmic features supporting lending decisions.
strategic_implication: Explainability and documentation should be part of FinNova's AI-lending design.

title: Account Aggregators can reduce loan-processing time
claim: Account Aggregators can substantially reduce the time required for loan processing.
evidence: RBI describes real-time financial-information sharing through AAs and explicitly connects it to faster loan processing.
strategic_implication: Consent-based financial-data integration is a credible lever for FinNova's lending transformation.

title: Consent-based data can enable frictionless digital credit
claim: RBI's Unified Lending Interface initiative aims to enable frictionless end-to-end digital credit using consent-based data and related services.
evidence: RBI describes ULI as a platform intended to leverage consent-based data to support frictionless digital credit.
strategic_implication: FinNova can model lending transformation around API-enabled, consent-based data flows.

title: AI can support credit assessment
claim: AI has potential to improve credit-risk assessment.
evidence: BIS identifies credit-risk assessment among financial-service areas where AI can improve quality and efficiency.
strategic_implication: AI-assisted underwriting is a valid transformation candidate, but must be paired with governance requirements.

title: Digital-finance growth increases the importance of effective complaint handling
claim: As digital financial services expand, accessible and efficient complaint handling becomes increasingly important.
evidence: World Bank guidance recommends functional, accessible and efficient complaint channels and clear escalation processes.
strategic_implication: Customer-service transformation should include complaint resolution and escalation, not just chatbot deflection.

title: Digital-credit complaint journeys can become fragmented
claim: Digital-credit customers may face fragmented complaint mechanisms across lenders, platforms, partners and other providers.
evidence: World Bank notes that multiple entities can create confusion about where complaints should be lodged and resolved.
strategic_implication: FinNova should design a unified complaint-intelligence workflow across its ecosystem.

title: AI can improve customer support
claim: GenAI-powered chatbots can assist customer service and potentially handle more complex customer tasks.
evidence: BIS describes AI-powered customer-service chatbots and their potential to break complex tasks into components.
strategic_implication: FinNova can explore AI-assisted support with human escalation for higher-risk cases.

title: Multilingual AI can reduce customer interaction friction
claim: AI-enabled multilingual chatbots and voice interfaces can make financial interactions simpler and more responsive.
evidence: BIS discusses multilingual and voice-based AI as a way to reduce paperwork and language-related friction.
strategic_implication: For a geographically diverse customer base, multilingual support can be a measurable CX transformation lever.

title: RBI received millions of customer complaints through ombudsman channels
claim: RBI reported 2.96 lakh complaints received at Ombudsman offices during 2024-25, with many related to loans/advances and digital banking products.
evidence: RBI Annual Report 2024-25 records 2.96 lakh complaints and identifies loans/advances and digital banking products as major complaint areas.
strategic_implication: Complaint volume and digital-banking issues justify customer-service analytics and faster resolution as a transformation dimension.

title: AI creates model, cyber and third-party risks in finance
claim: AI can amplify vulnerabilities involving third-party dependencies, cyber risk, market correlations and model risk.
evidence: FSB identifies these vulnerabilities while noting benefits such as efficiency, compliance, customisation and advanced analytics.
strategic_implication: FinNova's transformation portfolio needs explicit risk and dependency assessment for AI initiatives.

title: NIST AI RMF uses Govern, Map, Measure and Manage
source_name: National Institute of Standards and Technology
claim: The NIST AI Risk Management Framework organizes AI risk management into Govern, Map, Measure and Manage functions.
evidence: NIST describes these four functions as the core structure for managing AI risks across the lifecycle.
strategic_implication: FinNova can use these functions as a governance reference layer for evaluating proposed AI initiatives.

title: Trustworthy AI includes privacy, fairness and explainability
source_name: National Institute of Standards and Technology
claim: NIST identifies reliability, safety, security, accountability, transparency, explainability, privacy and fairness as trustworthiness characteristics.
evidence: NIST AI RMF FAQ lists these characteristics and recommends considering them throughout the AI lifecycle.
strategic_implication: FinNova's AI prioritisation model should score more than ROI; it should also account for trustworthiness and risk.

title: Financial-sector AI governance needs to evolve with AI adoption
claim: Authorities should monitor AI developments, assess policy-framework adequacy and enhance supervisory capabilities.
evidence: FSB calls for stronger monitoring and assessment as AI adoption in finance grows.
strategic_implication: FinNova should treat AI governance as a continuing capability rather than a one-time compliance checklist.

title: Regulators are examining AI's long-term impact on retail finance
claim: The FCA's 2026 Mills Review examines how AI may reshape retail financial services through 2030 and beyond.
evidence: The review covers technology evolution, firms and markets, consumers, risks, resilience and regulatory approaches.
strategic_implication: AI transformation should be evaluated against future market and regulatory change, not just current operational benefits.

title: Account Aggregators enable secure consent-based financial data sharing
claim: Account Aggregators enable customers to share financial information securely based on clear instructions.
evidence: RBI explains that AAs do not see or store the financial information and share it with financial institutions based on customer instructions.
strategic_implication: FinNova can build data-enabled products without assuming unrestricted ownership of all customer financial data.

title: Account Aggregator data can support broader financial services
claim: Digitally transmitted financial-asset information can support lending, credit monitoring, wealth management and personal finance management.
evidence: RBI identifies these use cases within its Account Aggregator explanation.
strategic_implication: FinNova can treat consented financial data as a platform capability supporting multiple products rather than only loan underwriting.

title: Digital-finance data can support credit scoring and fraud reduction
claim: New sources of data and data processing can support customer-centric products, credit scoring, KYC and fraud reduction.
evidence: World Bank discusses these benefits while also highlighting the need to manage consumer risks.
strategic_implication: FinNova's data strategy can connect lending, KYC and fraud use cases through governed data capabilities.

title: AI finance adoption increases dependence on data, cloud and third parties
claim: GenAI adoption in finance increases reliance on data, cloud services and third parties, creating governance and financial-stability considerations.
evidence: OECD recommends quality data, sound governance, privacy and ethics alongside monitoring concentration and application diversity.
strategic_implication: FinNova's data platform must include data quality, privacy and third-party dependency controls.

title: UPI operates at very large transaction scale
claim: UPI recorded 22.716 billion transactions worth approximately ₹28.92 trillion in June 2026.
evidence: NPCI's published monthly statistics report 22,716.07 million transactions and ₹2,892,138.67 crore in June 2026.
strategic_implication: At this ecosystem scale, payment reliability, fraud monitoring and analytics are strategically significant capabilities.

title: AI consumer risks include bias, privacy and unreliable outputs
claim: AI in finance can create risks involving data protection, privacy, bias, discrimination and unreliable outputs.
evidence: OECD highlights these risks alongside benefits such as accessibility, timely information, cost-effective services and improved user experiences.
strategic_implication: FinNova should include consumer-risk controls in AI use-case prioritisation and deployment readiness.
